title: Bayberry and soy pillar candle
subtitle: A traditional blend in a freestanding pillar form
excerpt: A freestanding pillar candle of bayberry wax blended with soy wax, scented with cedarwood and frankincense. Bayberry gives a pale sage-green colour and a faint balsamic scent. Makes one 50 mm diameter pillar.
sourceNotes: Bayberry wax (Myrica cerifera) properties and traditional use: documented in 18th-century American colonial accounts of bayberry tallow candles. Modern bayberry wax properties: general candlemaking supplier data sheets. Soy-bayberry blend ratios: standard candle formulation practice (5 to 15% bayberry in a soy base for a freestanding pillar).

recipe.yieldDescription: 1 pillar candle (50 mm diameter, ~180 mm tall, ~40 burn hours)
recipe.batchNotes: Two or three pillars per session.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Five years unlit in a cool, dark place. Bayberry wax is extremely stable; the cedarwood and frankincense essential oils hold their note well in a hard wax blend. Discard only if the wax surface cracks deeply or the wick has migrated out of centre.

glossaryTerms.definition: A pale sage-green wax rendered from the waxy coat of bayberry (Myrica) fruit. One of the oldest candle materials in North American tradition. High melt point (around 47°C), balsamic scent, and a distinctive green colour. Blended with soy at 10 to 15% for pillar candles to give structure without brittleness.

content.text: A freestanding pillar candle that blends
into a soy base for a pale sage-green pillar with a faint resinous scent. At 10% in a soy base it gives colour and a slightly harder burn. Cedarwood and frankincense essential oils deepen the note.
Pillar candles must be burned on a heatproof surface in a candle holder that catches drips. Never leave unattended.

items.prepNote: soy wax base; 90% of wax weight
10% of wax weight; gives colour and balsamic note
2% of total wax weight; deepens the resinous base
pre-tabbed wick sized for a 50 mm diameter pillar; thread through the mould base hole before pouring

content.text: Thread the wick through the base hole of the aluminium mould. Pull tight and secure the base end with mould sealer putty. Rest the top end of the wick across a wooden skewer laid across the open top of the mould so it stays centred.

Melt the soy wax and bayberry wax together in the pouring pitcher over a bain-marie. Stir until both are fully liquid and combined. Cool to 65°C. Add the cedarwood and frankincense essential oils and stir for one minute.

Pour the wax blend into the mould in one steady flow. Leave to cool at room temperature. A sinkhole will form around the wick as the wax contracts; poke through the surface with a skewer and top up with a second small pour once the first layer is firm. Repeat if needed.

Leave for at least 24 hours before unmoulding. Remove the mould sealer putty and slide the candle out of the aluminium mould. The metal surface transfers a smooth finish. Trim the wick to 5 mm. Cure for one week.
Five years in a cool, dark place. Bayberry-soy blend is stable and does not bloom or yellow as easily as pure soy pillars.
